question: Why does a backend need rate limiting at all, and what does ratelimit-kit give a Node app?
answer_hinglish:
Rate limiting ka seedha matlab hai: ek client (IP, user, account) ek time period mein kitni requests ya kitna kaam kar sakta hai, uski upper limit. Do wajah se chahiye. Pehli, capacity: ek client (ya ek buggy script) itni requests bhej de ki baaki sab users ke liye server slow ho jaaye -- limit lagane se ek client ka load baaki sab ko nahi girata. Doosri, security: login, OTP, password reset jaise endpoints par attacker guesses try karta hai; '5 tries per 15 minutes' jaisi limit brute force ko practically bekaar bana deti hai.

ratelimit-kit ek TypeScript library hai jo yeh kisi bhi Node app ko deti hai. Do algorithms hain -- token bucket (burst up to capacity, phir steady rate) aur sliding window counter (about N per window). Dono do jagah chal sakte hain: MemoryStore mein (ek process, dev / tests / single instance) ya RedisStore mein, jahan poora read-decide-write ek Lua script mein atomically chalta hai, toh kitne bhi app instances ek hi limit share karte hain.

Important design point: library ka koi runtime dependency nahi hai. Aap apna Redis client pass karte ho (ioredis ka adapter included hai). Lua scripts project 1 (projects/01-rate-limiter) se unchanged copy kiye gaye hain, kyunki wahan woh already tested the. README ke hisaab se 91 tests pass hote hain aur 51 mutation checks mein se 49 caught, 2 equivalent hain. Npm par publish nahi hai.
why_needed: Bina limit ke ek client poore server ki capacity kha sakta hai, aur security endpoints par unlimited guesses milte hain. Har app mein yeh khud likhna galti-prone hai (race conditions, wrong client IP), isliye ek tested library.
real_world_analogy: Building ki lift mein 'max 8 log' likha hota hai. Lift kharab na ho aur sabko chance mile, isliye limit hai -- kisi ek group ko poori lift bhar ke baar baar upar-neeche nahi jaane dete.
how_it_works: Har request par app ek key banata hai (jaise `email:a@b.com` ya `ip:1.2.3.4`), RateLimiter.consume(key, cost) call karta hai, aur ek Decision milta hai: allowed hai ya nahi, kitna bacha, kab retry karo. Allowed na ho toh adapter 429 + Retry-After bhejta hai.
in_this_project: README ka 'Use it' section do limiters dikhata hai: loginLimit = slidingWindow({ limit: 5, windowMs: 15 * 60_000 }) RedisStore par prefix 'rl:login:' ke saath, aur apiLimit = tokenBucket({ capacity: 20, refillPerSec: 5 }) MemoryStore par prefix 'rl:api:'. src/index.ts sab public cheezein export karta hai: tokenBucket, slidingWindow, RateLimiter, MemoryStore, RedisStore, ioredisClient, FailoverStore. Express aur NestJS adapters alag entry points hain (ratelimit-kit/express, ratelimit-kit/nestjs).
advantages: Ek client baaki sab ki capacity nahi kha sakta
Brute force (login / OTP) practically band
Same API memory aur Redis dono ke liye
disadvantages: Har limit ek aur config hai jise tune karna padta hai
Galat key (galat client IP) ho toh limit ya toh bypass hoti hai ya sab ek saath limit ho jaate hain
common_mistakes: Sirf per-IP limit lagana aur per-account limit bhool jaana (attacker IP badal leta hai)
Multi-instance deployment mein MemoryStore use karna -- N instances = up to N x limit
Har request par naya RateLimiter banana (state share hi nahi hoti)
follow_up_questions: What is the difference between a capacity limit and a security limit?
Why is a per-instance in-memory counter not enough behind a load balancer?
What should the client receive when it is limited?

question: Explain the token bucket algorithm: what do capacity and refillPerSec mean?
answer_hinglish:
Token bucket mein har client ka ek bucket hota hai jisme maximum `capacity` tokens aa sakte hain. Har request `cost` tokens leti hai (default 1). Bucket `refillPerSec` tokens per second ki rate se bharta hai, lekin capacity se upar kabhi nahi jaata.

Iska behaviour do hisson mein samjho. Burst: agar client kaafi der se idle hai, bucket full hai, toh woh ek saath `capacity` requests bhej sakta hai -- sab allowed. Steady state: burst ke baad bucket khaali hai, ab sirf utni requests allowed hain jitne tokens refill hote hain, yaani `refillPerSec` per second. Toh tokenBucket({ capacity: 20, refillPerSec: 5 }) ka matlab: 'ek saath 20 tak, phir lagatar 5 per second'.

Is project mein do details important hain. Ek, naya key full bucket se shuru hota hai (`state?.tokens ?? capacity`) -- naya user pehli request par hi deny na ho. Mutation L6 (naya bucket khaali shuru ho) ne 20 tests fail kiye. Do, request ya toh poore `cost` tokens leti hai ya kuch nahi: agar tokens < cost toh deny, aur koi token nahi kat-ta.

Yeh algorithm zyada tar API limits ke liye sahi hai (PLAN.md: 'most API limits'), kyunki real clients bursty hote hain -- page load par 10 calls ek saath, phir kuch der kuch nahi. Ek strict 'per second' counter us burst ko galat tareeke se deny karta.
why_needed: Real traffic bursty hota hai. Ek algorithm chahiye jo short burst allow kare par long-term average rate ko bandh ke rakhe.
real_world_analogy: Metro card ki tarah socho jisme max 20 rides ka balance aa sakta hai aur har second automatically thoda recharge hota hai. Ek saath 20 rides le lo, phir utni hi jitni recharge hoti hai.
how_it_works: State per key: { tokens, ts }. Har request par: elapsed = now - ts, tokens = min(capacity, tokens + elapsed * rate / 1000), phir agar tokens >= cost toh tokens -= cost aur allowed, warna denied with retry. Naya state { tokens, ts: now } save hota hai.
in_this_project: src/algorithms.ts::tokenBucket options validate karta hai (positive() -- capacity aur refillPerSec dono finite aur > 0, warna RateLimitError 'must be a positive number'). Algorithm ka `limit` = capacity. Redis twin src/lua/token_bucket.lua hai jo state ek hash {tokens, ts} mein rakhta hai. Test 'allows a burst of `capacity`, then denies with the exact wait for one token' (capacity 5, rate 1): 5 allowed with remaining 4..0, phir { allowed: false, limit: 5, remaining: 0, retryAfterMs: 1000, resetMs: 5000 }.
advantages: Bursts allowed, average rate bounded
Sirf do numbers per key (tokens, ts) -- O(1) memory
Variable cost naturally fit hota hai
disadvantages: 'N per window' jaisi exact guarantee nahi deta -- ek window mein capacity + rate x time tak ho sakta hai
Do parameters tune karne padte hain
common_mistakes: capacity ko 'per second limit' samajh lena
Naya bucket khaali shuru karna (pehli request hi deny)
Deny par bhi tokens kaat lena

question: What is a sliding window counter and how is it different from a plain fixed window?
answer_hinglish:
Sliding window counter 'about N requests per window' wali limit deta hai, lekin window ke edge par burst ke bina. Fixed window mein har client ka ek counter hota hai jo har window (jaise har minute) par zero ho jaata hai. Problem: limit 10/min hai toh client 0:59 par 10 aur 1:00 par 10 bhej sakta hai -- 2 second mein 20, double limit. Yeh edge burst hai.

Sliding window counter do counters rakhta hai: current window ka count aur previous window ka count. Phir estimate karta hai ki pichhle `windowMs` ke sliding window mein kitni requests hui:

estimate = cur + prev x (window - elapsed) / window

yahan elapsed = current window shuru hue kitna time hua. Matlab previous window ka utna hissa count hota hai jitna abhi bhi sliding window ke andar hai. Current window mein 25% aage ho toh previous ka 75% count hota hai. Agar estimate + cost > limit toh deny.

Yeh approximate hai -- assume karta hai ki previous window ki requests evenly spread thi. Lekin memory O(1) hai (do counters), jabki exact sliding LOG har request ka timestamp rakhta hai. PLAN.md ke hisaab se yeh login / OTP style limits ke liye hai: '5 tries per 15 minutes' smooth tareeke se, bina edge ke double burst ke.
why_needed: 'N per window' ek natural business rule hai (5 login tries per 15 min), lekin fixed window edge par 2N allow kar deta hai. Sliding counter woh gap bandh karta hai bina har request store kiye.
real_world_analogy: Train ke coach mein 'last 1 ghante mein kitne log chadhe' ka andaza: pichhle ghante ka total aur is ghante ka total, aur pichhle ghante ka utna hissa jitna abhi bhi last 60 minute mein aata hai.
how_it_works: Window boundaries fixed hain (curStart = now - now % window). Counter current window ke key par INCRBY hota hai. Previous window ka count weight (window - elapsed)/window se multiply hota hai. Do window peeche wala count bilkul count nahi hota.
in_this_project: src/algorithms.ts::slidingWindow aur src/lua/sliding_counter.lua. Lua mein do keys banti hain: `<key>:<cur_start>` aur `<key>:<prev_start>`. Test 'weights the previous window: 10 last window, 25% into this one -> 7.5 still count' limit 10 ke saath: 1 + 7.5 = 8.5 -> remaining 1, 2 + 7.5 = 9.5 -> remaining 0, teesri request 10.5 > 10 -> denied, retryAfterMs 3000.
code_example:
-- real, src/lua/sliding_counter.lua (trimmed)
local cur_start = now - (now % window)
local prev_start = cur_start - window
local cur = tonumber(redis.call('GET', KEYS[1] .. ':' .. cur_start) or '0')
local prev = tonumber(redis.call('GET', KEYS[1] .. ':' .. prev_start) or '0')
local elapsed = now - cur_start
local weight = (window - elapsed) / window
local estimated = cur + prev * weight
advantages: Window edge par double burst nahi
O(1) memory per client (do counters)
'N per window' rule ke kareeb
disadvantages: Approximate -- exact sirf jab previous window ki requests evenly spread ho
Token bucket jaisa burst-then-rate model nahi
common_mistakes: Previous window ko weight dena bhool jaana (fixed window ban jaata hai -- mutation S1)
Do window purane count ko bhi previous maan lena (mutation S4)
Ise exact samajhna

Why does a denied request not increment the counter?
How is retryAfterMs computed for a denied request?

question: What does the Decision type contain and how does a caller use each field?
answer_hinglish:
Decision woh object hai jo har consume() call ka jawab hai. src/types.ts mein iske fields hain:

- allowed: request jaane do ya nahi.
- limit: token bucket mein capacity, sliding window mein limit per window.
- remaining: is request ke BAAD kitne whole units bache (floor kiya hua).
- retryAfterMs: allowed ho toh 0; warna kitne ms baad YAHI cost allowed hogi.
- resetMs: token bucket mein kab tak bucket poora bhar jaayega; sliding window mein current window kab khatam hogi.
- degraded?: sirf tab true jab decision FailoverStore ke fallback se aaya (Redis fail hua tha), warna field hi absent hai.

Caller ka kaam simple hai: allowed false ho toh 429 bhejo aur Retry-After header retryAfterMs se banao. Stage 2 adapters (src/adapters/http.ts ka rateLimitHeaders) yeh khud karte hain: RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, RateLimit-Reset (resetMs/1000 rounded UP) aur deny par Retry-After (kam se kam 1 second).

Ek subtle baat: retryAfterMs 'is cost ke liye' hai. Agar client cost 4 maang raha hai aur sirf 3 tokens hain, toh retry 1 token ke refill ka time hai, sirf 'koi bhi request' ka nahi. Aur fields readonly hain -- Decision ek value hai, mutate karne ke liye nahi. Memory aur Redis store dono exactly yahi shape return karte hain; RedisStore Lua ke 4-element reply ko toDecision() se isi mein badalta hai.
why_needed: Sirf true/false kaafi nahi: client ko batana padta hai kab retry kare, aur dashboards / headers ko bacha hua quota chahiye. Ek common type se memory, Redis aur adapters sab ek hi language bolte hain.
real_world_analogy: Bank ATM ki slip: transaction hua ya nahi, account limit kya hai, kitna bacha, aur agar mana hua toh kab dobara try karo.
how_it_works: Algorithm ka step() (ya Lua script) Decision banata hai. RedisStore Lua reply {allowed, remaining, retry, reset} ko toDecision() mein check karta hai (array, length 4, sab numbers) aur limit algorithm se jodta hai. FailoverStore fallback par { ...decision, degraded: true } return karta hai.
in_this_project: src/types.ts::Decision mein comments har field ka matlab likhte hain. src/redis-store.ts::toDecision unexpected reply shape par error throw karta hai -- guess nahi karta (test 'an unexpected reply shape is an error, not a guess', mutation R3). src/adapters/http.ts::rateLimitHeaders Decision se headers banata hai.
advantages: Ek shape memory, Redis aur fallback sab ke liye
Headers seedhe isi se bante hain
degraded flag se pata chalta hai ki limit per-instance thi
disadvantages: remaining whole units hai -- fractional token info chhup jaati hai
retryAfterMs ek estimate hai; doosre requests beech mein tokens le sakte hain
common_mistakes: retryAfterMs ko seconds samajh lena (yeh ms hai)
Retry-After ko round DOWN karna (0 second = turant retry -- mutation H6)
resetMs aur retryAfterMs ko same cheez samajhna
follow_up_questions: Why is retryAfterMs defined per cost and not per single unit?
Why is degraded an optional field and not always false?

question: What does `cost` mean in consume(key, cost), and how do the two algorithms treat a request that costs more than one unit?
answer_hinglish:
cost ka matlab hai: yeh request kitne units ki hai. Default 1 hai. Lekin har request barabar mehngi nahi hoti -- README ka example: ek bulk endpoint 5 cost kar sakta hai. Toh consume(key, 5) bolta hai 'is request ke liye 5 units chahiye'.

Token bucket mein: agar bucket mein tokens >= cost hain toh cost tokens kat-te hain aur allowed. Warna DENY aur ek bhi token nahi kat-ta -- all or nothing. Test 'cost > 1 takes several tokens at once; a denied request takes none': capacity 10 -- consume 7 -> remaining 3, consume 4 -> denied, remaining abhi bhi 3, retryAfterMs 1000 (1 token chahiye, rate 1/s), phir consume 3 -> allowed, remaining 0. Mutation L4 ('needs MORE than cost tokens', yaani > ki jagah >=) ne 12 tests fail kiye.

Sliding window mein: condition hai estimate + cost > limit toh deny; allowed ho toh counter INCRBY cost se badhta hai. Denied request kuch count nahi karta.

Validation RateLimiter.consume mein hoti hai: cost ek safe integer >= 1 hona chahiye (0 ya 1.5 RateLimitError), aur cost limit se zyada ho toh bhi error, kyunki woh kabhi allowed ho hi nahi sakti. Express / NestJS adapters mein cost(req) option hai jo har request ka cost nikalta hai.
why_needed: Ek 'GET item' aur ek '500 items export' server par same load nahi daalte. Cost se ek hi limit dono ko fair tareeke se gin sakti hai.
real_world_analogy: Toll plaza: car ka ek token, truck ke teen. Truck ke liye teen token nahi hain toh truck ruk jaata hai -- aadha toll nahi liya jaata.
how_it_works: Cost dono algorithms mein 'tokens chahiye' / 'counter mein kitna judega' ban jaata hai. Lua mein ARGV[4] cost hai; RedisStore args ke end mein String(cost) append karta hai.
in_this_project: src/algorithms.ts mein `if (tokens >= cost)` aur `if (estimated + cost > limit)`. src/limiter.ts::RateLimiter cost validate karta hai. src/redis-store.ts mein `const args = [...algorithm.args(), now, String(cost)]`. Adapter option src/adapters/express.ts mein `cost?: (req: IncomingMessage) => number; // default 1`.
advantages: Mehngi requests ko zyada gina ja sakta hai
All-or-nothing: aadhi request ka matlab nahi banta
Ek limit mein mixed endpoints
disadvantages: Cost function galat ho toh limit ya toh bahut tight ya bahut loose
Cost > limit ek error hai -- caller ko pehle se dhyan rakhna padta hai
common_mistakes: Deny par partial tokens kaat lena
Fractional cost (1.5) bhejna -- RateLimitError
Cost ko user input se seedha lena (client khud cost 1 bata dega)

question: What is the 'edge burst' problem of a fixed window limiter, and how do the two algorithms in this project avoid it?
answer_hinglish:
Fixed window mein time ko fixed buckets mein kaato -- jaise 12:00:00-12:00:59, 12:01:00-12:01:59 -- aur har bucket mein max N. Problem window ke boundary par hai: client 12:00:59 par N requests bhejta hai (pehli window ka poora quota) aur 12:01:00 par phir N (nayi window, counter zero). Do second mein 2N requests -- jo 'N per minute' rule ka double hai. Isi ko edge burst kehte hain. PLAN.md fixed window ko isi wajah se chhodta hai: 'fixed window has the edge burst'.

Sliding window counter isse aise bachta hai: nayi window shuru hote hi previous window ka count gayab nahi hota; woh weight (window - elapsed)/window ke saath count hota hai. 12:01:00 par weight 1 hai, toh pichhle N poore count hote hain -- turant N aur nahi mil sakte. Test 'a denied request does not count' mein exactly yahi hai: limit 1, window 10 mein 1 allowed, window 11 ke start par request denied (weight 1 -> 1, still full).

Token bucket mein window ka concept hi nahi hai. Max burst hamesha capacity tak hai; uske baad sirf refill rate. Koi boundary nahi jahan counter achanak zero ho.

Interview mein balanced bolna: fixed window bekaar nahi hai -- sabse simple aur sasta hai, aur project 1 mein fixed_window.lua abhi bhi hai. Is library ne bas use offer nahi kiya.
why_needed: Agar limit business ya security rule hai (5 login tries per 15 min), toh boundary par 10 tries allow karna rule tod deta hai.
real_world_analogy: Mahine ke data pack ki tarah: 30 tareekh ko poora pack use karo, 1 tareekh ko naya pack -- do din mein do mahine ka data.
how_it_works: Fixed window: count[window_start] += cost, compare with N. Sliding counter: same window keys, lekin decision mein previous window ka weighted hissa bhi judta hai, toh boundary par estimate continuous rehta hai.
in_this_project: Project 1 mein projects/01-rate-limiter/ratelimiter/limiter/lua/fixed_window.lua hai; is library mein sirf token_bucket.lua aur sliding_counter.lua copy hue. Mutation S1 ('previous window not weighted') sliding window ko effectively fixed window bana deta hai -- 2 tests fail hue.
advantages: Sliding counter aur token bucket dono boundary par smooth hain
Rule ka matlab ('N per window') zyada sach rehta hai
disadvantages: Smooth hone ki keemat: sliding counter approximate hai
Fixed window se thoda zyada logic aur do keys
common_mistakes: Socho ki fixed window ka problem sirf theory hai -- bots exactly boundary par hi bhejte hain
Sliding counter ko exact maan lena

question: What is a rate-limit key and why does RateLimiter add a prefix per limit?
answer_hinglish:
Key woh string hai jo batati hai 'kisko limit kar rahe hain'. README ke examples: `email:${email.toLowerCase()}`, ek IP key jaisa 'ip:1.2.3.4', ya 'user:42:otp'. Har key ka apna bucket / window hota hai -- test 'keys are independent': capacity 1 par 'a' allowed, 'b' allowed, 'a' phir denied.

Prefix kyun? Ek hi app mein kai limits hoti hain: ek general API limit, ek login limit. Dono ke liye key same ho sakti hai (wahi IP). Agar dono same store aur same key use karein toh unka state mix ho jaayega -- login ki tries API ke tokens kha lengi, ya ulta. Isliye har RateLimiter ek prefix rakhta hai aur store ko `prefix + key` bhejta hai: 'rl:login:ip:1.2.3.4' aur 'rl:api:ip:1.2.3.4' alag cheezein hain. Default prefix 'rl:' hai.

Test 'prefixes keys (default rl:) so different limits never share state' ek recording store se dekhta hai ki keys ['rl:ip:1.2.3.4', 'rl:login:ip:1.2.3.4'] gayi. Mutation Q1 (prefix apply nahi) ne 5 tests fail kiye.

Redis mein yeh aur important hai, kyunki Redis bahut saari cheezon ke beech share hota hai; prefix rate-limit keys ko baaki data se alag namespace mein rakhta hai. Ek baat dhyan rakhni: do limits jinka algorithm alag hai (token bucket hash vs sliding window string keys) same Redis key par aayein toh WRONGTYPE jaise errors aa sakte hain -- prefix yeh bhi rokta hai.
why_needed: Ek app mein kai limits hoti hain aur client identity same hoti hai. Namespace ke bina limits ek doosre ka state kha jaati hain.
real_world_analogy: Ek hi customer ka bank mein savings aur loan account -- dono ka number alag prefix se hota hai, warna ek ki entry doosre mein chali jaaye.
how_it_works: RateLimiter constructor mein `this.prefix = options.prefix ?? "rl:"`. consume() validation ke baad `this.options.store.consume(this.options.algorithm, this.prefix + key, cost)` call karta hai.
in_this_project: src/limiter.ts::RateLimiterOptions mein comment: 'one prefix per limit, so a login limit and an API limit for the same user never share state'. Key validation bhi yahin: non-empty aur max 512 characters (MAX_KEY_LENGTH).
advantages: Limits ek doosre se isolated
Redis mein rate-limit keys ek namespace mein (debug / cleanup easy)
Same store kai limiters share kar sakte hain
disadvantages: Prefix choose karna caller ki zimmedari hai -- do limiters same prefix dein toh phir mix
Lambi prefix + key Redis memory thodi badhati hai
common_mistakes: Do alag limits ko same prefix dena
Key mein normalise na karna (Email vs email -- README toLowerCase karta hai)
Unbounded user input ko key banana bina length limit ke

question: How does the token bucket refill 'lazily' without any timer, and why is that the right design?
answer_hinglish:
Lazy refill ka matlab: koi background timer tokens nahi daalta. Hum sirf do cheezein store karte hain -- kitne tokens the (tokens) aur kab (ts). Jab agli request aati hai, tab calculate karte hain ki beech mein kitna time guzra aur utne mein kitne tokens drip hue hote:

tokens = min(capacity, tokens + elapsed * rate / 1000)

elapsed ms mein hai, rate tokens per second, isliye /1000. min() se capacity par cap lagta hai. Phir naya { tokens, ts: now } save hota hai.

Yeh sahi design kyun hai? Socho 1 lakh clients hain. Timer-based refill ka matlab har client ke liye har tick par ek write -- chahe client idle ho. Lazy refill mein kaam sirf request aane par hota hai, O(1), aur idle clients ka koi cost nahi. Redis mein yeh aur zaroori hai: ek Lua script mein hi read, refill, decide, write ho jaata hai -- koi cron nahi, koi race nahi.

Test 'refills lazily at refillPerSec (half a second = half a token: still denied, retry 500)' -- capacity 2, rate 2: do requests se bucket khaali, 250 ms baad 0.5 token -> denied with retryAfterMs 250, aur 250 ms aur baad 1 token -> allowed, remaining 0. Yaani tokens fractional hote hain; 0.5 token kaafi nahi. Mutation L2 (refill capacity par cap nahi) ne 3 tests fail kiye -- test 'never refills above capacity' ek ghante idle ke baad bhi remaining 2 expect karta hai (capacity 3).
why_needed: Timer har client ke liye kaam karta hai chahe woh idle ho; lazy calculation sirf request par kaam karta hai aur ek atomic script mein fit hota hai.
real_world_analogy: Paani ki tanki jisme nal hamesha chalta hai. Aap har second tanki nahi dekhte; jab paani chahiye tab dekhte ho 'pichhli baar kitna tha, kitni der hui, toh ab kitna hoga' -- aur tanki overflow nahi hoti.
how_it_works: elapsed = max(now - ts, 0); tokens = min(capacity, tokens + elapsed * rate / 1000); allowed if tokens >= cost. State hamesha 'last seen' ke time par snapshot hai, aur har read par aage project hota hai.
in_this_project: src/lua/token_bucket.lua mein comment: '-- Lazy refill: we never run a timer, we just compute how much would have dripped in.' TypeScript twin src/algorithms.ts::tokenBucket mein same do lines hain. Redis key par PEXPIRE capacity*1000/rate + 1000 lagta hai, kyunki itne idle time ke baad bucket full hi hota.
code_example:
-- real, src/lua/token_bucket.lua
-- Lazy refill: we never run a timer, we just compute how much would have dripped in.
local elapsed = math.max(now - ts, 0)
tokens = math.min(capacity, tokens + elapsed * rate / 1000)
advantages: Idle clients ka zero cost
Ek atomic step mein refill + decide
Arbitrary precision rate (0.001/s bhi chalta hai)
disadvantages: Clock par depend hai -- clock jumps ko handle karna padta hai
Fractional tokens store hote hain, toh precision ka dhyan (Lua tostring 14 digits)
common_mistakes: setInterval se refill karna
Cap lagana bhool jaana (idle client ke paas unlimited burst)
ms aur seconds mix karna (/1000 bhool jaana)

question: How are retryAfterMs and resetMs computed in the token bucket, and why is the retry rounded up?
answer_hinglish:
Do alag sawaal hain. retryAfterMs: 'is cost ke liye kab tak rukna padega?' Agar tokens < cost, toh (cost - tokens) aur tokens chahiye, aur rate tokens per second se aate hain, toh:

retry = ceil((cost - tokens) * 1000 / rate)

resetMs: 'bucket poora kab bharega?'

reset = ceil((capacity - tokens) * 1000 / rate)

yeh request ke baad wale tokens par hai, chahe allowed ho ya denied.

Round UP kyun? Agar retry round down ho, toh client thoda jaldi wapas aayega, tab tak poora token nahi bana hoga, aur phir deny -- ek bekaar request aur ek galat promise. Ceil ka matlab hai 'is time par pakka mil jaayega' (agar beech mein koi aur token na le). Mutation L5 ('retry rounded down') test ne pakda. HTTP level par bhi yahi rule: rateLimitHeaders mein Retry-After = max(1, ceil(retryAfterMs/1000)) aur RateLimit-Reset bhi ceil (mutations H6, H7).

Concrete numbers: test mein capacity 5, rate 1, paanch requests ke baad tokens 0 -> retryAfterMs = ceil(1 * 1000 / 1) = 1000, resetMs = ceil(5 * 1000 / 1) = 5000. Refill test mein capacity 2, rate 2, 250 ms baad 0.5 token -> retry = ceil(0.5 * 1000 / 2) = 250.

Ek subtle point: reply full-precision tokens se nikalta hai, stored rounded value se nahi -- parity test ne isi par 1 ms ka fark pakda tha.

question: Walk through the sliding window counter's estimate and retry math with the numbers from the tests.
answer_hinglish:
Formula: curStart = now - now % window, elapsed = now - curStart, weight = (window - elapsed) / window, estimate = cur + prev x weight. Deny agar estimate + cost > limit.

Test ke numbers: limit 10, window 60 000 ms. Window 10 mein 10 requests allowed. Ab time 11 x W + W/4 hai -- current window mein 25% aage. weight = 0.75, toh prev ka 10 x 0.75 = 7.5 count hota hai.
- Pehli request: 0 + 7.5 + 1 = 8.5 <= 10 -> allowed, cur = 1, remaining = floor(10 - 8.5) = 1.
- Doosri: 1 + 7.5 + 1 = 9.5 -> allowed, remaining floor(0.5) = 0.
- Teesri: 2 + 7.5 + 1 = 10.5 > 10 -> denied.

Retry: do candidates. (1) window khatam hone tak: window - elapsed = 45 000 ms. (2) previous window ka weighted hissa itna ghate ki jagah ban jaaye: needed = estimate + cost - limit = 0.5. Prev har ms mein prev/window ghat-ta hai, toh ms = ceil(needed / prev x window) = ceil(0.5 / 10 x 60 000) = 3000. Chhota wala chuna jaata hai -> retryAfterMs 3000. Exactly yahi test assert karta hai.

Agar prev = 0 hai toh sirf candidate (1) bachta hai -- test 'allows `limit` in a fresh window' mein denial par retryAfterMs = W. Final retry par max(retry, 1) lagta hai; README isse mutation S6 ke liye equivalent bataata hai kyunki dono candidates already >= 1 ms hain. Mutation S5 (retry previous window ki decay ignore kare) 2 tests ne pakda.
why_needed: Retry math galat ho toh client ya toh 45 second bekaar rukta hai jab 3 second kaafi the, ya bahut jaldi aakar phir deny hota hai.
real_world_analogy: Raat ko bheed wali dukaan: pichhle ghante ke log dheere dheere nikal rahe hain. Aapko poora ghanta khatam hone ka wait nahi karna -- bas itna ki ek jagah khaali ho.
how_it_works: Decay linear hai: previous window ka contribution prev x (window - elapsed)/window, jo har ms prev/window kam hota hai. Isliye 'needed' ko us rate se divide karke time milta hai.
in_this_project: src/algorithms.ts::slidingWindow aur src/lua/sliding_counter.lua line by line same hain. Lua comment: '-- prev contributes prev/window per ms'. Allowed par remaining = max(floor(limit - (cur + prev*weight)), 0); resetMs dono cases mein window - elapsed.

question: Why does the sliding window counter not count a denied request, and what goes wrong if it did?
answer_hinglish:
Rule simple hai: denied request state ko kuch nahi badalti. Lua script mein deny branch `return {0, ...}` se INCRBY se pehle hi nikal jaata hai, aur TypeScript step() denied case mein purana state hi return karta hai ('A denied request changes nothing (the Lua script returns before INCRBY)').

Agar denied requests count hoti toh kya hota? Socho login limit 5 per 15 min. Attacker ya ek buggy client limit ke baad bhi har second retry karta hai. Har denied request counter badhaati, toh counter limit se bahut upar chala jaata. Current window khatam hone ke baad yeh bada count 'previous' ban jaata aur agli poori window weight ke saath user ko block rakhta. Matlab ek client jo bas zyada retry karta hai, uska lockout lambha aur lambha hota jaata -- aur genuine user jo baar baar 'Login' daba raha hai woh khud ko lock kar leta. Limit ka matlab 'N allowed per window' hai, 'N attempts' nahi.

Test 'a denied request does not count' iski edge tak check karta hai: limit 1, window 10 mein 1 allowed + 5 denied. Window 11 ke start par denied (prev 1 x weight 1). Aadhi window par 0.5 + 1 = 1.5 > 1 denied. 12W - 1 par bhi denied, kyunki 1 x 1/60000 + 1 = 1.0000167 > 1 -- yeh precision edge hai. 12W par window 10 do peeche hai aur window 11 mein 0 allowed tha -> allowed. Agar denied count hote toh window 11 mein count hota aur yeh request bhi deny hoti. Mutation S3 (denied counted) 2 tests fail, aur Lua version ka mutation U2 real-Redis tests ne pakda.

Trade-off: ek client limit par hammer karta rahe toh Redis / memory par har denied request ka read ka cost phir bhi hai -- bas write nahi.
why_needed: Limit ka semantic 'allowed per window' hona chahiye. Denied ko ginna retries ko punish karta hai aur lockout unbounded bana deta hai.
real_world_analogy: Club ka bouncer: andar 50 log max. Jo bahar se mana kiya gaya, use andar ki ginti mein nahi jodte -- warna bahar khade logon ki wajah se andar jagah hone par bhi koi andar na jaa paaye.
how_it_works: Deny branch: koi INCRBY nahi, koi PEXPIRE nahi; reply {0, remaining, max(retry,1), window - elapsed}. TS: `return { state: state ?? { start: curStart, count: 0, prevCount: 0 }, decision }`.

README: 'A denied request is not counted'. Token bucket mein bhi denied request koi token nahi leta, lekin woh state ka ts aur refilled tokens likhta hai (Lua HSET dono cases mein).

Genuine users retry karke khud ko lock nahi karte
Deny path par Redis write nahi

Denied requests ka read cost phir bhi lagta hai

Penalty chahiye toh usse algorithm mein chhupana -- alag 'ban' limit banana behtar hai

question: What is the Algorithm interface and why does every algorithm have both a step() function and a Lua twin?
answer_hinglish:
src/types.ts ka Algorithm<S> interface ek algorithm ko do roop mein describe karta hai: name, limit, luaFile (src/lua/ mein kaunsi script), args() (ARGV[1], ARGV[2] -- RedisStore isme now_ms aur cost append karta hai), step(state, now, cost) jo TypeScript version hai aur { state, decision } return karta hai.

step() pure function jaisa hai: purana state (undefined = kabhi dekha nahi), time aur cost do -- naya state aur decision lo. MemoryStore bas Map se state nikalta hai, step chalata hai, naya state wapas rakhta hai. RedisStore step() ko chhoota bhi nahi; woh luaFile load karta hai, args() + now + cost ke saath EVALSHA karta hai.

Do versions kyun? PLAN.md ka decision: agar memory store ek 'alag, simpler implementation' hota, toh dev / tests (memory) se production (Redis) par jaate hi behaviour chupchaap badal jaata. Isliye dono versions ko IDENTICAL decisions dene hain, aur test/redis.test.ts mein parity test seeded random sequence (time jumps, 3 keys, cost 1-3) dono par chalata hai: har algorithm ke liye 3 seeds x 200 steps, aur check karta hai ki allowed aur denied dono outcomes exercise hue.

Stores generic hain: Store interface ka consume<S>(algorithm, key, cost). Isliye naya algorithm jodne ke liye store badalna nahi padta -- bas ek Algorithm object aur ek Lua file.

Ek honest note: pehle interface mein stateTtlMs() bhi tha aur dono algorithms use implement karte the, lekin koi store use nahi karta tha -- MemoryStore ka expiry hata diya gaya tha aur Lua scripts apna PEXPIRE khud calculate karti hain. Interview bank likhte waqt yeh dead code pakda gaya aur interface aur dono algorithms se hata diya. Usi review mein types.ts ka purana comment ('test/parity.test.ts', jo file exist hi nahi karti) bhi theek hua -- ab woh test/redis.test.ts ke parity tests ki taraf point karta hai.

question: How does MemoryStore implement a bounded LRU with a plain JavaScript Map?
answer_hinglish:
JavaScript Map apne keys ko insertion order mein yaad rakhta hai. MemoryStore isi ka faayda uthata hai: Map ka pehla key = least recently used, aakhri = most recently used.

consume() mein teen kaam hote hain:
1. state nikalo aur algorithm.step() chalao.
2. key ko delete karke dobara set karo -- isse woh Map ke end par chala jaata hai (most recently used). Sirf set() karne se order nahi badalta agar key pehle se hai; isliye delete + set.
3. Agar size maxKeys se zyada ho gaya, toh entries.keys().next().value -- yaani sabse purana key -- delete karo.

Sab O(1) hai: koi linked list, koi alag data structure nahi. Default maxKeys 100 000 hai; constructor check karta hai ki woh safe integer >= 1 ho, warna RangeError (test 0, -1, 1.5 reject karta hai).

Tests: 'keeps at most maxKeys keys, dropping the least recently used': maxKeys 2 -- a, b, phir a (denied, lekin ab a most recent), phir c -> b evict hota hai. Size 2, a ka state bacha (denied), b fresh (allowed). Dhyan do: denied request bhi recency refresh karti hai, kyunki har consume re-insert karta hai. Doosra test: 100 000 distinct keys, maxKeys 1000 -> size exactly 1000. Mutations M1 (kabhi evict nahi) aur M2 (recency refresh nahi) dono pakde gaye.
why_needed: Keys client se aati hain (IPs); unbounded Map ek memory attack hai. LRU sabse active clients ko rakhta hai aur sabse purane ko chhodta hai.
real_world_analogy: Chhota parking lot jisme ek hi gate hai: jo gaadi sabse pehle aayi aur tab se hili nahi, woh sabse pehle bahar. Jo gaadi chali, woh line ke end mein chali jaati hai.
how_it_works: Map insertion order + delete/set = move to back. Overflow par front se ek delete. Eviction sirf insertion ke time, ek key per insert.

question: Project 1 had five algorithms. Why does ratelimit-kit ship only token bucket and sliding window counter?
answer_hinglish:
PLAN.md ka pehla decision: 'Two algorithms, not five.' Project 1 (projects/01-rate-limiter) mein fixed window, sliding log, sliding counter, token bucket aur leaky bucket -- paanchon Lua scripts the. Library ke liye do chune gaye, har ek ka ek clear use case:

- Token bucket: bursts up to capacity, then steady rate -- zyada tar API limits.
- Sliding window counter: about N per window, smooth at edges -- login / OTP style limits.

Baaki teen kyun nahi:
- Fixed window: edge burst. Boundary par 2N allow ho sakta hai, jo 'N per window' ko tod deta hai. Aur jo ise sasta banata hai, sliding counter almost utna hi sasta hai.
- Sliding log: har request ka timestamp store karta hai, toh memory per client requests ke saath badhti hai. Exact hai, lekin 'sliding log needs memory per request' -- high limit par mehnga, aur memory attack surface bhi.
- Leaky bucket: PLAN ke words mein 'a queue, not a limiter'. Woh requests ko ek constant rate par drain karta hai -- shaping hai, jahan request ko rukna padta hai; jabki ek HTTP limiter ko turant allow/deny chahiye.

Library design ka principle: kam options, har option clearly justified. Har algorithm do baar likha jaata hai (TS + Lua) aur parity-tested hota hai, toh har extra algorithm maintenance aur test cost double karta hai. Do algorithms almost saare real cases cover karte hain.
why_needed: Library ka har option ek decision hai jo user ko lena padta hai aur ek cheez jo maintain karni padti hai. Clear 'kab kaunsa' wale do options paanch confusing options se behtar.
real_world_analogy: Ek achhe restaurant ka chhota menu: 2 dishes jo perfect banti hain, 15 jo theek-thaak.

question: The sliding window counter is approximate. When is the error largest, and why is that acceptable here compared with an exact sliding log?
answer_hinglish:
Counter assume karta hai ki previous window ki requests poori window mein evenly spread thi. Isliye woh prev ka linear share count karta hai. Error tab sabse bada hota hai jab previous window ki requests ek kone mein clustered thi.

Example: limit 10, window 60 s. Previous window ke aakhri second mein 10 requests aayi. Ab current window mein 30 s aage. Counter bolta hai prev ka 50% = 5 count hoga, toh 5 aur allowed. Lekin asli sliding 60 s window mein woh 10 requests abhi bhi poori andar hain -- exact log 0 allow karta. Ulta case: previous ki 10 requests uske pehle second mein thi; asli window mein unme se koi andar nahi, lekin counter 5 gin raha hai -- zaroorat se zyada strict. Toh error dono direction mein ho sakta hai.

Acceptable kyun? Teen wajah. Ek, memory: counter per client do integers rakhta hai, sliding log har request ka timestamp -- limit 1000 ho toh 1000 entries per client, aur keys client se aati hain. Do, edge burst ka sabse bura case (fixed window ka 2N) yahan bahut damp ho jaata hai. Teen, login / OTP jaise use cases mein 'about N per window' kaafi hai -- README khud 'about N per window' bolta hai.

Lua comment kehta hai 'This is the approach Cloudflare described publicly; error is small when traffic is smooth.' Is project ne error khud measure nahi kiya -- yeh dhyan rakho interview mein.
why_needed: Exactness ki keemat memory hai. Ek limiter jiske keys attacker control karta hai, wahan O(1) state ek security property bhi hai.
real_world_analogy: Highway toll par 'pichhle ghante kitni gaadiyan' ka andaza: pichhle ghante ka total x jitna hissa abhi bhi window mein hai. Har gaadi ka time likhna exact hai, par register bahut mota ho jaata.

question: MemoryStore evicts the least recently used key at maxKeys. Why bound memory at all, and what is the cost of evicting a client?
answer_hinglish:
Bound isliye kyunki rate-limit keys client se aati hain -- IP, user id, email. Agar Map unbounded ho, toh attacker har request alag key se bhej sakta hai (IPv6 mein lakhon addresses, ya fake emails), aur har key ek entry banayegi. Kuch der mein process ki memory khatam -- rate limiter khud DoS vector ban gaya. src/memory-store.ts ka comment yahi kehta hai: 'without a bound a flood of distinct keys is a memory attack.'

Isliye maxKeys (default 100 000) aur LRU eviction. Test: 100 000 distinct keys, maxKeys 1000 -> exactly 1000 bache.

Keemat: jab ek key evict hoti hai, us client ka state chala jaata hai. Agli request par woh 'naya' lagta hai -- full bucket ya khaali window. Matlab uska limit RESET ho gaya. Test yeh explicitly dikhata hai: b evict hua aur phir allowed. README isse 'the trade-off for bounded memory' bolta hai.

Kya yeh attack ban sakta hai? Haan, theory mein: attacker bahut saare naye keys bhej ke ek victim key (jaise apni hi) ko LRU se bahar dhakka de, phir fresh limit le. Lekin uske liye use maxKeys jitne distinct keys bhejne padenge, aur un sab requests par bhi limit chal rahi hai. LRU yeh ensure karta hai ki jo clients abhi active hain (jo limit ke kareeb hain) woh sabse last mein jaayein.

Alternative -- 'full ho toh naye keys deny karo' -- naye genuine users ko block karta. Isliye reset chuna gaya.
why_needed: Ek limiter jo khud unbounded memory kha sakta hai, woh attack surface hai. Bounded memory ek hard safety property hai.
real_world_analogy: Chhote hotel ke 100 kamre: full ho jaaye toh sabse purana check-in wala, jo mahinon se dikha nahi, uska register entry hata do. Agar woh lautega toh naye guest ki tarah treat hoga.

Mutations M1, M2 pakde gaye.

question: MemoryStore originally had a per-key expiry. Why was it removed, and what does that tell you about mutation testing?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle version mein MemoryStore ek lazy expiry check rakhta tha -- Redis ke PEXPIRE ki tarah, idle key ko expired maan lo. Phir mutation testing hua: ek deliberate bug ek time par daalo, poora suite chalao, dekho koi test fail hota hai ya nahi. Mutation M3 ne expiry ko ignore karwaya -- aur koi test fail nahi hua. Mutation survive kar gaya.

Survive karne ke do matlab ho sakte hain: ya test kamzor hai, ya code redundant hai. Yahan dusra tha. Socho kyun: token bucket mein idle key ke tokens refill hote hote capacity par cap ho jaate hain -- full bucket = naya key (naya key bhi full se shuru hota hai). Sliding window mein do ya zyada window purana state na current match karta hai na previous, toh cur = 0, prev = 0 -- jaise koi state hi nahi. Matlab dono algorithms long-idle state ko already 'no state' jaisa treat karte hain. Expiry sirf memory free karti -- aur memory toh maxKeys already bound karta hai.

Isliye expiry hata di gayi, aur ek test add hua jo is property ko pakka karta hai: 'a long-idle key behaves exactly like a new one (no expiry needed)': ek din baad idle key ka Decision fresh key ke Decision ke toEqual hai, dono algorithms ke liye.

Lesson: mutation testing sirf tests ko judge nahi karta, design ko bhi. Ek surviving mutant ya toh missing test dikhata hai, ya dead / redundant code. Dono case mein action alag hai: test add karo, ya code hatao aur property ko test se lock karo. Line coverage yeh nahi pakad sakta -- expiry code chal raha tha, bas kuch badal nahi raha tha.
why_needed: Har extra branch ek bug ka mauka hai. Jo code kisi decision ko nahi badalta, use hatana aur property ko test se pakka karna system ko simpler aur sahi rakhta hai.
real_world_analogy: Gaadi mein ek extra lock jo kabhi lagta hi nahi kyunki doosra lock already wahi kaam karta hai. Mechanic ne use nikal diya aur check kiya ki gaadi utni hi safe hai.
how_it_works: Token bucket: min(capacity, tokens + elapsed*rate/1000) bade elapsed par capacity -> fresh key jaisa. Sliding window: state.start na curStart, na curStart - window -> cur = prev = 0. Isliye expiry check ka koi observable effect nahi.

README Mutation section: 'M3 (the memory store ignored its expiry) survived and showed the expiry was redundant -- removed; L3 survived and got a sharper test.' Test test/limiter.test.ts mein 'a long-idle key behaves exactly like a new one'. Redis scripts mein PEXPIRE abhi bhi hai -- wahan woh memory free karne ke liye zaroori hai (mutation U3 'no expiry on the token bucket key' pakda gaya). Algorithm.stateTtlMs() expiry hatne ke baad interface mein bacha reh gaya tha aur koi store use nahi karta tha -- dead code samajh ke woh bhi baad mein hata diya gaya.

Property ab explicit test se locked
Memory bound ka ek hi mechanism (maxKeys)
disadvantages: Idle keys tab tak memory lete hain jab tak LRU unhe na nikaale

Coverage ko quality maan lena
Redis ka PEXPIRE bhi 'redundant' samajh ke hata dena -- wahan woh memory ke liye zaroori hai

question: Why does RateLimiter treat a cost above the limit as an error instead of simply denying the request?
answer_hinglish:
Socho token bucket capacity 5 hai aur koi consume(key, 6) bolta hai. Bucket kabhi 5 se zyada tokens nahi rakhta, toh 6 tokens kabhi available nahi honge. Agar hum ise normal denial ki tarah treat karte, toh algorithm retryAfterMs calculate karta -- jaise 'ek second baad aao'. Client ek second baad aata, phir deny, phir naya retry... hamesha ke liye. README ke words: 'a denial with a retry time would be a lie.'

Sliding window mein bhi same: estimate kam se kam 0 hai, toh 0 + 6 > 5 hamesha deny.

Isliye RateLimiter.consume yeh case store tak jaane se PEHLE pakad leta hai aur RateLimitError throw karta hai: 'cost 6 exceeds the limit 5'. Yeh bug hai -- caller ka config ya cost function galat hai -- client ka misbehaviour nahi. Isliye 429 nahi, error.

Yeh choice adapters ke saath bhi jodti hai: RateLimitError kabhi fail-open nahi hota. Express aur Nest dono mein `if (error instanceof RateLimitError || ...) throw error;` -- chahe onStoreError 'allow' ho, bug error handler tak jaata hai (mutations O1, O7). Kyunki agar bug ko 'allow' kar diya, toh woh chupchaap production mein rahega aur limit kaam hi nahi karegi.

Boundary test: cost = limit allowed hai ('a key of exactly 512 characters and a cost equal to the limit are fine'). Mutation Q2 (cost above limit not rejected) 3 tests ne pakda.
why_needed: Ek 'kabhi na hone wali' cheez ke liye retry time dena client ko infinite loop mein daalta hai aur asli bug (config) ko chhupata hai.
real_world_analogy: Lift mein 'max 8 log' hai aur 10 log ka group kehta hai 'kab jagah hogi?'. Sahi jawab 'kabhi nahi, group todo' hai -- 'agli baar' bolna jhooth hai.
how_it_works: Validation order: key type/empty, key length, cost integer >= 1, cost <= algorithm.limit. Sab store call se pehle; recording store test check karta hai ki koi key store tak nahi pahunchi.

PLAN.md decision: 'A cost above the limit is an error, not a denial with a retry time that can never work.'

Fail-open se bug kabhi chhupta nahi

question: In tokenBucket's step(), why is the stored token count rounded with luaToString while the reply uses the full-precision value?
answer_hinglish:
Yeh parity ki kahani hai. Redis ka Lua token count hash mein `tostring(tokens)` se store karta hai. Redis Lua mein tostring '%.14g' format use karta hai -- yaani sirf 14 significant digits. Toh jo Redis mein store hota hai woh full double nahi, 14 digit rounded number hai. Agli request par wahi rounded value padhi jaati hai.

Agar TypeScript MemoryStore full precision store karta, toh kuch steps ke baad dono ke tokens thode alag hote, aur kabhi na kabhi ek 'tokens >= cost' boundary par ek allow kare, doosra deny. Isliye src/algorithms.ts mein `luaToString = (x) => Number(x.toPrecision(14))` hai, aur state `{ tokens: luaToString(tokens), ts: now }` store hota hai. Mutation L1 (full precision store) parity test mein fail hua. Unit test: luaToString(0.1 + 0.2) = 0.3, luaToString(1/3) = 0.33333333333333, luaToString(4.999999999999999) = 5.

Lekin reply? Lua script `remaining` aur `reset` LOCAL variable `tokens` se nikalta hai, jo full precision hai -- tostring sirf HSET ke argument par lagta hai. Pehle TypeScript version ne dono jagah rounded value use ki. Parity test seed 1 ke step 91 par fail hua: resetMs 1135 vs 1136. Ek ceil ke boundary par 14-digit rounding ne 1 ms ka fark daala. Fix: reply full value se, store rounded value. Code comment: 'The reply uses the FULL-precision value (the Lua variable); only the STORED value is rounded by tostring().'

Interview point: 'same algorithm' ka matlab same formula nahi, same numeric semantics bhi hai -- storage format ki rounding bhi.
why_needed: Memory aur Redis ko bit-for-bit same decisions dene hain; warna dev aur production alag behave karte.
real_world_analogy: Do accountant same hisaab karte hain, lekin ek register mein 2 decimal tak likhta hai. Doosre ko bhi register mein waise hi likhna padega, par customer ko bill dono full calculation se dete hain.
how_it_works: Flow: refill -> decide -> decision from `tokens` (full) -> state.tokens = luaToString(tokens). Agli step rounded value se shuru hoti hai, bilkul jaise Lua HMGET rounded string padhta hai.
in_this_project: src/algorithms.ts::luaToString aur tokenBucket ka last part. src/lua/token_bucket.lua: `redis.call('HSET', KEYS[1], 'tokens', tostring(tokens), 'ts', tostring(now))` aur reply `{allowed, math.floor(tokens), retry, reset}`. Note: Lua file ka purana comment 'Store state with full precision (tostring keeps the fraction)' project 1 se unchanged hai -- fraction rakhta hai, lekin sirf 14 significant digits; isliye file ke top par ab ek note hai jo yeh correct karta hai ('tostring keeps 14 significant digits (%.14g)') aur luaToString aur README ke 'Parity' section ki taraf point karta hai.

disadvantages: Redis implementation detail (%.14g) TS code mein leak hota hai
Agar Redis version tostring ka format badle toh parity toot sakti hai

Parity test na hona aur yeh 1 ms bug production mein milna

question: Walk through RateLimiter.consume. Why does all validation happen before the store is touched, and why is the key capped at 512 characters?
answer_hinglish:
RateLimiter.consume(key, cost = 1) chaar checks karta hai, phir store ko call karta hai:
1. key string ho aur empty na ho.
2. key 512 characters se lambi na ho (MAX_KEY_LENGTH).
3. cost safe integer ho aur >= 1 (0 ya 1.5 reject).
4. cost algorithm.limit se zyada na ho.
Sab fail cases RateLimitError throw karte hain. Phir `store.consume(algorithm, prefix + key, cost)`.

Store se pehle kyun? Teen wajah. Ek, bekaar Redis round trip nahi -- invalid input ke liye network call ka koi matlab nahi. Do, galat data store mein nahi jaata: ek fractional cost Lua mein INCRBY ko fail karega (INCRBY integer maangta hai), ya empty key state ko ek ajeeb jagah likhega. Teen, error type clear rehta hai: RateLimitError matlab 'caller ka bug', jabki store se aaya error matlab 'infrastructure'. Adapters isi fark par fail-open decide karte hain -- RateLimitError kabhi fail-open nahi.

Test yeh exactly check karta hai: ek recording store har key note karta hai, aur har invalid case ke baad `expect(keys).toEqual([])` -- store ko chhua tak nahi.

512 ka cap kyun? Keys aksar client data se banti hain (email, header). Bina cap ke koi 1 MB ka email bhej ke har request par 1 MB ki Redis key bana sakta hai -- memory attack. Boundary test: exactly 512 allowed, 513 rejected; mutation Q3 (off by one) pakda gaya.
why_needed: Validation ek jagah aur pehle -- taaki store implementations simple rahein aur bugs infrastructure errors se alag pehchaane jaayein.
real_world_analogy: Courier office counter par hi parcel ka size aur address check hota hai, truck mein load karne se pehle -- galat parcel truck tak jaaye hi kyun.
how_it_works: Sequential guard clauses; pehla fail hone wala check throw karta hai. limit getter algorithm.limit return karta hai (adapters headers ke liye use karte hain).
in_this_project: src/limiter.ts::RateLimiter aur `const MAX_KEY_LENGTH = 512;`. test/limiter.test.ts ka it.each: empty key, 513 chars, cost 0, cost 1.5, cost 6 above limit 5 -- sab 'rejects %s before touching the store'.

Store simple -- validated input maan sakta hai
Key size ka DoS band
disadvantages: Prefix length cap mein count nahi hota (cap sirf key par hai)
Validation async function ke andar hai, toh errors rejected promise ke roop mein aate hain, sync throw nahi
common_mistakes: Validation store ke andar duplicate karna
Key length ko cap na karna
RateLimitError ko generic Error bana dena (fail-open logic toot jaata)

Should the 512-character cap include the prefix?

question: The token bucket uses Math.max(now - ts, 0). What exactly happens when the clock goes backwards, and what does that code NOT protect against?
answer_hinglish:
Lazy refill time ke difference par depend karta hai: tokens + elapsed * rate / 1000. Agar clock peeche chala jaaye (NTP correction, alag servers ke alag clocks), toh now - ts negative hoga aur bina guard ke tokens GHAT jaayenge. Isliye elapsed = max(now - ts, 0): backward jump par refill zero.

Test 'a clock going backwards neither adds nor REMOVES tokens': capacity 10, rate 1, ek request (9 bache), clock -5000 ms. Bina guard ke 9 - 5 = 4, phir request -> 3. Guard ke saath 9 - 1 = 8. Mutation L3 pehle survive hua tha, phir test sharper banaya gaya (README).

Ab jo yeh code NAHI karta -- yeh interview bank ki code review mein mila, aur README ab ise ek 'Limitation (not changed)' ki tarah likhta hai. Step ke end mein state ts: now ke saath save hota hai, yaani PEECHE wala time. Agar baad mein clock wapas aage sahi time par aa jaaye, toh agli request elapsed ko is peeche wale ts se naapegi -- matlab woh 5 second jo pehle hi refill mein gine ja chuke the, dobara gine jaayenge: recovery ke baad extra refill (capacity par capped). Lua script mein bhi same: HSET ts tostring(now).

Sliding window mein: backward jump se curStart purane window par aa sakta hai. TypeScript state sirf ek window yaad rakhta hai, jabki Redis mein purani window ki key abhi bhi ho sakti hai (PEXPIRE 2 windows) -- toh is case mein dono implementations alag decision de sakte hain. Parity test sirf aage badhte time (t += random >= 0) se chalta hai, toh yeh case cover nahi hai.

Practical defense: RedisStore by default Redis ka apna TIME use karta hai, ek hi clock -- app servers ke drift ka sawaal hi nahi.
why_needed: Production mein clocks jump karte hain. Limiter ko us par predictable rehna chahiye -- na client ko saza, na free tokens.
real_world_analogy: Pani ki meter reading: agar meter galti se peeche ghoom jaaye toh aap customer ko negative paani ka credit nahi dete -- bas us reading par bill zero.
how_it_works: Guard sirf us ek step ka elapsed clamp karta hai. ts hamesha 'latest seen now' nahi, balki 'is request ka now' hai, isliye backward step ts ko bhi peeche le jaata hai.

README: token bucket ka '**Limitation** (found while writing the interview bank, not changed)' -- double refill, fix `max(ts, now)` store karna jo project 1 ki Lua badalta; aur Parity ka 'Scope' note (sirf forward time tested; backwards clock par sliding window alag ho sakta hai).

question: In slidingWindow's step(), how does a single in-memory state object reproduce what Redis stores in two keys, and why must windowMs be an integer?
answer_hinglish:
Redis mein sliding window do keys mein rehta hai: `<key>:<cur_start>` aur `<key>:<prev_start>`. Purani keys PEXPIRE (window * 2) se khud chali jaati hain. MemoryStore ke paas ek key ke liye ek hi value hai, toh TypeScript state { start, count, prevCount } rakhta hai: count = jis window ka start `start` hai uska count, prevCount = usse pehle wali window ka.

step() har baar reconstruct karta hai 'Redis ko abhi kya milta':
- state.start === curStart -> hum usi window mein hain: cur = count, prev = prevCount.
- state.start === curStart - window -> stored window ab previous ban gayi: prev = count, cur = 0.
- warna (do ya zyada window purana) -> dono 0 -- jaise Redis mein dono keys expire ho chuki hoti.
Comment exactly yahi kehta hai: 'What Redis would find under the keys for the current and the previous window.' Allowed par naya state { start: curStart, count: cur, prevCount: prev }.

Mutation S4 ('a window two back still counts as previous') 4 tests ne pakda -- test 'a window two or more back no longer counts'.

windowMs integer kyun? curStart = now - now % window. Redis mein yeh number key ke naam mein jaata hai (`KEYS[1] .. ':' .. cur_start`). Fractional window par curStart fractional hoga, aur Lua ka number-to-string conversion aur JS ka number formatting alag ho sakte hain, plus % floats par rounding error deta hai -- key names aur boundaries unstable. Isliye slidingWindow 'windowMs must be an integer' RateLimitError deta hai (test 10.5 reject karta hai). Limit fractional ho sakta hai (positive() sirf > 0 check karta hai), window nahi.
why_needed: Memory version ko Redis ke multi-key layout jaisa hi behave karna hai bina multiple keys banaye; integer window key names ko stable rakhta hai.
real_world_analogy: Do register (is mahine aur pichhle mahine) ki jagah ek card jisme 'kaunsa mahina, is mahine ka total, pichhle ka total' likha ho -- har baar card dekh ke samjho ki mahina badal gaya ya nahi.
how_it_works: Window alignment epoch ke hisaab se hai (now % window), client-specific nahi. Isliye har client ki windows same boundaries par badalti hain.

question: Exercise: add a fixed-window algorithm to ratelimit-kit that implements the Algorithm interface, with its Lua twin and a vitest test. What must you be careful about?
answer_hinglish:
Task ka matlab hai library ke contract ko follow karna: ek Algorithm<S> object (name, limit, luaFile, args, step) aur src/lua/ mein ek script jo exactly same decisions de. Is library mein fixed window implement NAHI hai -- PLAN ne use jaan-boojh kar chhoda tha (edge burst) -- toh yeh exercise sirf practice ke liye hai, aur test edge burst ko document bhi karta hai.

Steps:
1. State { start, count }. step() mein start = now - now % window; agar state.start === start toh count, warna 0 (purani window bhool jao -- expiry ki zaroorat nahi, wahi 'idle == fresh' property).
2. Deny agar count + cost > limit; denied kuch count nahi karta (sliding window wala rule). retryAfterMs = resetMs = window - (now - start), jo hamesha >= 1 hai.
3. Allowed par count + cost store karo.
4. Lua twin: same ARGV layout (limit, window, now_ms ya '' for Redis TIME, cost) kyunki RedisStore args() ke baad now aur cost append karta hai. Deny branch INCRBY se PEHLE return. PEXPIRE window.
5. Reply 4 integers {allowed, remaining, retry, reset} -- toDecision isi shape ko maangta hai, aur Redis Lua floats ko integer reply mein truncate karta hai, isliye floor / integer values hi bhejo.
6. Test: memory unit test + test/redis.test.ts ke parity() mein naya run.

Careful points: windowMs integer (key name mein jaata hai), Lua file build par copy hoti hai (scripts/copy-lua.mjs poora src/lua/ copy karta hai, toh naya file automatically dist mein), aur cost > limit RateLimiter pehle hi reject karega.

real_world_analogy: Naya dish menu mein jodna: recipe card (step), restaurant kitchen ka version (Lua), aur dono ka taste test (parity) -- teeno ke bina dish menu par nahi aati.
how_it_works: MemoryStore aur RedisStore dono generic hain, toh koi store code nahi badalta. RedisStore luaFile se script padhta hai, sha1 nikalta hai, EVALSHA karta hai, NOSCRIPT par load karke retry.
in_this_project: Contract src/types.ts::Algorithm mein hai; existing examples src/algorithms.ts::tokenBucket aur slidingWindow. Project 1 ka apna fixed window projects/01-rate-limiter/ratelimiter/limiter/lua/fixed_window.lua mein hai, lekin uska ARGV layout is library se match karta hai ya nahi, woh verify karna padega -- isliye yahan naya likha. Neeche ka code illustrative hai, repo mein nahi.
advantages: Store code untouched -- interface ka faayda
Parity test se Lua aur TS ka match prove
Test edge burst ko document karta hai
disadvantages: Fixed window edge burst rakhta hai -- isliye library mein nahi
Ek aur Lua file maintain karni
common_mistakes: Deny par bhi INCRBY karna
Lua reply mein float bhejna (Redis truncate karega)
ARGV order badal dena (RedisStore hamesha now aur cost ko 3rd/4th par append karta hai)
Parity test na jodna
follow_up_questions: How would you make this cluster-safe?
Why is retryAfterMs equal to resetMs here but not in the sliding window?

advanced.failure_scenarios: Boundary par synchronized clients (sab bots minute ke start par) -- sab ek saath allowed. Lua aur TS ke beech koi chhota fark (jaise remaining floor) -- parity test pakdega.

question: Exercise: write a per-route cost function for an export endpoint using the Express adapter's `cost` option, and a vitest test for it.
answer_hinglish:
Express adapter ka `rateLimit(limiter, { cost })` har request ke liye `cost(req)` call karta hai aur result limiter.consume(key, cost) mein jaata hai (default 1). Task: GET /export?rows=N ke liye cost = har shuru hue 100 rows ka 1 unit.

Dhyan dene wali baatein, sab is library ke code se aati hain:
1. Cost integer >= 1 hona chahiye -- RateLimiter Number.isSafeInteger aur >= 1 check karta hai. Toh Math.ceil aur kam se kam 1. Garbage input (rows=abc) par 1.
2. Cost limit se zyada nahi hona chahiye -- warna RateLimitError, jo adapter mein 'error' ban ke error handler tak jaata hai (500), onStoreError 'allow' ke saath bhi. Toh ya toh clamp karo ya bahut badi request ko limiter se PEHLE 413 se reject karo. Example dono karta hai: 2000 rows se upar 413, aur cost function limit par clamp.
3. Cost function throw na kare: adapter cost ko store wale try ke BAHAR compute karta hai, aur poora async block .catch(next) mein hai, toh throw error handler tak jaata hai (500) -- onStoreError 'allow' ke saath bhi kabhi fail open nahi. (Pehle stage-3 version mein cost try ke andar tha aur 'allow' par throwing cost function fail open ho jaata tha; interview bank likhte waqt pakda, fix hua, aur har adapter ke liye ek test hai.)
4. Cost client ke kehne par trust nahi -- yahan rows query se aata hai, lekin cost server decide karta hai rows se, client 'cost=1' nahi bata sakta.

Test do level par: pure function test (rows -> units, clamp) aur ek real Express app test jo headers check kare. Capacity 20, rate 1: rows=1500 -> cost 15 -> RateLimit-Remaining 5; phir rows=1000 -> cost 10 > 5 -> 429, Retry-After = ceil(5 tokens / 1 per s) = 5. Code illustrative hai, repo mein nahi; repo ke express.test.ts mein sirf 'cost' option ka basic test hai (mutation E3 'cost option ignored' 2 tests ne pakda).
why_needed: Endpoints ka load barabar nahi hota. Cost function se ek hi limit mehngi requests ko zyada ginti hai, bina alag limiter banaye.
real_world_analogy: Courier ka rate: ek chitthi ek unit, 5 kilo ka parcel 5 unit -- lekin truck ki capacity se bada parcel counter par hi mana, 'baad mein aana' nahi.
how_it_works: Middleware: key = keyFn(req); cost = options.cost?.(req) ?? 1 (try ke bahar); try { decision = await limiter.consume(key, cost) }; headers set; allowed -> next(), warna 429 + Retry-After.
in_this_project: src/adapters/express.ts::rateLimit mein `const cost = options.cost?.(req) ?? 1;` try ke bahar (comment: 'a throwing cost function is a bug in the app, never a store error to fail open on'), phir try mein `decision = await limiter.consume(key, cost);`. RateLimitMiddlewareOptions mein `cost?: (req: IncomingMessage) => number; // default 1`. NestJS guard (src/adapters/nestjs.ts) mein bhi same `cost` option hai. RateLimiter ka `limit` getter clamp ke liye use ho sakta hai.
advantages: Ek limiter, fair weighting
Cost server decide karta hai, client nahi
Clamp + 413 se bugs aur abuse dono handle
disadvantages: Cost function ek aur cheez jise test karna padta hai
Galat mapping (rows ka approximate) limit ko loose ya tight karti hai
common_mistakes: Cost ko clamp na karna -> RateLimitError -> 500
Cost ko client header se lena
Float cost return karna (Math.ceil bhool jaana)
follow_up_questions: What happens in the adapter if the cost function throws?
Should the 413 check go before or after the limiter, and why?
How would you do the same with the NestJS @RateLimit decorator?

question: Design the limits for a login endpoint and a public API with this library: which algorithm, which key, which store, and why?
answer_hinglish:
Do alag goals hain, isliye do alag limits.

Login (security): sliding window counter. Rule 'N tries per window' natural hai, edge burst nahi, aur denied tries count nahi hoti -- toh genuine user retry karke khud ko lock nahi karta. Token bucket yahan kamzor hai: idle ke baad poora capacity burst mil jaata hai. README example: slidingWindow({ limit: 5, windowMs: 15 * 60_000 }), prefix 'rl:login:'. Key: do limits stack karo -- per account (README ka byEmail: email string ho toh `email:${email.trim().toLowerCase()}`, warna undefined -- `email:${undefined}` nahi, jo har bina-email request ko ek shared bucket mein daal deta) taaki IP badal ke ek account par guesses na hon, aur per IP taaki ek IP bahut saare accounts try na kare. NestJS mein do @RateLimit decorators, Express mein do middleware -- 'stacked limiters all apply; the first denial wins'. Store: RedisStore -- multiple instances par MemoryStore N x limit deta (load test: MemoryStore ke saath 3 instances par limit 500 -> 1116 allowed; Redis ke saath exactly 500). Redis down par fail CLOSED (onStoreError 'deny' -> 503), taaki attacker ko outage mein unlimited guesses na milein.

Public API (capacity): token bucket -- clients bursty hote hain, capacity burst aur refill steady rate. README: tokenBucket({ capacity: 20, refillPerSec: 5 }). Key: authenticated user id, warna keyByIp({ trustedProxies: n }) -- n exactly utna jitne proxies aapke hain. Bulk endpoints ke liye cost(req). Store: RedisStore, aur Redis down par fail OPEN ('allow') -- sabko mana karna briefly unlimited se bura hai. Behtar: FailoverStore with MemoryStore fallback -- degraded par bhi per-instance limit.

Cost-above-limit dhyan rakho: login par cost hamesha 1.
why_needed: Ek hi 'rate limit' setting sab endpoints par lagana ya toh security kamzor karta hai ya API users ko bina wajah rokta hai. Har limit ka goal (security vs capacity) algorithm, key, store aur failure mode tay karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank branch: locker room mein entry ki strict ginti (security, gadbad ho toh band), aur cash counter par line management (capacity, gadbad ho toh bhi counter chalta rahe).
how_it_works: Har limit = ek RateLimiter (algorithm + store + prefix). Adapter key function se client pehchanta hai, cost se units, onStoreError se failure mode. Stacked limiters ek ke baad ek chalte hain.
in_this_project: README 'Use it' aur 'When Redis is down' sections exactly yeh do limits dikhate hain (loginLimit sliding window on Redis, apiLimit token bucket; onStoreError 'deny' for /login, 'allow' for /api). src/adapters/http.ts ka OnStoreError comment bhi capacity vs security ka fark likhta hai. Load test numbers bench/reference-results/2026-11-23-win32-load-run1.json se hain; throughput numbers README ke hisaab se VALID NAHI hain (PC 90-100% CPU par tha), isliye sirf correctness quote karo.
advantages: Har limit apne goal ke hisaab se tuned
Per-account + per-IP stacking dono attack shapes rokta hai
Failure mode per limit explicit
disadvantages: Zyada limiters = zyada Redis calls per request
Stacked limiters mein pehla limiter consume kar chuka hota hai jab doosra deny kare
common_mistakes: Login par sirf per-IP limit
Sab limits ko same onStoreError dena
X-Forwarded-For ko bina trustedProxies ke trust karna
Multi-instance par MemoryStore
follow_up_questions: Why fail closed with 503 and not 429 for login?
What does an attacker gain if trustedProxies is set too high?
How would you prevent one user's lockout from being triggered by an attacker who knows their email?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Sliding window login ke liye smooth, strict-ish; token bucket API ke liye burst-friendly. Fail closed security ke liye sahi par Redis outage mein login band; fail open capacity ke liye sahi par outage mein unlimited -- FailoverStore beech ka raasta (degraded per-instance limit).
advanced.failure_scenarios: Redis down: login 503 (users login nahi kar paate), API allow ya degraded. Attacker victim ke email par galat passwords bhej ke victim ko lock kar sakta hai -- per-account limit ka known side effect; is library mein iska solution (jaise per-account + per-IP combination ke liye alag logic) nahi hai.
advanced.alternatives: API gateway / nginx limit_req (infra level), CAPTCHA after N failures, exponential backoff per account -- yeh library mein nahi.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x traffic par Redis per request 1-2 script calls; hot keys (ek shared limit) ek Redis shard par. 100x par Redis Cluster -- sliding window ki undeclared keys ki wajah se README ke hisaab se NOT tested, hash tag chahiye.
advanced.production_improvements: Per-limit metrics (allowed / denied / degraded), denials par alerting, aur ek idle machine par valid throughput / latency measurement -- README isse NOT implemented bolta hai.

question: How do you prove that a TypeScript implementation and a Redis Lua implementation of the same algorithm stay equivalent, and where does this project's proof stop?
answer_hinglish:
Is project ka jawab: differential testing with a seeded random sequence, against a REAL Redis. test/redis.test.ts ka parity() function ek fake clock `t` rakhta hai jo dono stores ko diya jaata hai (MemoryStore({ now }) aur RedisStore(..., { now })). Har step par time random aage badhta hai, 3 keys mein se ek chuni jaati hai, cost 1-3 random, aur dono limiters se same request -- `expect(b, `step ${i}, seed ${seed}`).toEqual(a)`. Har algorithm ke liye 3 seeds x 200 steps = 600 steps, aur assertion ki allowed aur denied dono hue (warna test sirf ek path cover karta). PRNG mulberry32 seeded hai -- fail ho toh seed aur step number se exactly replay.

Yeh kaam karta hai: is test ne first version ka 1 ms resetMs bug pakda (seed 1, step 91), aur mutation L1 (precision) bhi. Lua mutations U1-U3 real Redis tests ne pakde.

Proof kahan rukta hai -- yeh interview mein khud bolna chahiye:
1. Time sirf aage badhta hai (Math.floor(rand() * maxAdvanceMs) >= 0). Backward clocks parity mein nahi; sliding window mein mere code reading ke hisaab se TS aur Redis yahan alag ho sakte hain.
2. Ek hi parameter set per algorithm (capacity 5 / rate 3, limit 6 / window 1000). Extreme rates ya bade numbers tested nahi.
3. Tests injected clock use karte hain; production Redis TIME use karta hai -- woh path alag test hota hai (empty time argument, expiry set).
4. Redis na ho toh tests SKIP hote hain (printed notice ke saath), pass nahi.
5. Random testing sampling hai, proof nahi -- formal equivalence nahi.

PLAN ka reasoning: switching memory -> Redis 'would change behaviour silently' bina iske.
why_needed: Do implementations ka ek hi spec ho toh sabse sasta aur strong check unhe same inputs par chalana aur outputs compare karna hai -- hand-written cases woh corners miss karte hain jo random sequences pakadte hain.
real_world_analogy: Do translators ek hi kitaab translate karte hain. Aap random pages chun ke dono ke translation compare karte ho; har page check nahi kiya, lekin jo farak mila woh asli bug hai.
how_it_works: Differential / model-based testing: MemoryStore ka step() reference model, Redis Lua system under test (ya ulta). Seeded PRNG reproducibility deta hai; 'both outcomes exercised' assertion vacuous pass se bachata hai.
in_this_project: test/redis.test.ts: `async function parity<S>(name, algorithm, seed, steps, maxAdvanceMs)`, token bucket seeds [1, 2, 3] maxAdvance 700 ms, sliding window seeds [4, 5, 6] maxAdvance 400 ms. README 'Parity' section (uska 'Scope' note bhi: random sequences sirf time AAGE le jaati hain; backwards clock par sliding window ke dono versions alag ho sakte hain -- not tested, not fixed). src/types.ts ka comment ab 'the parity tests in test/redis.test.ts' bolta hai (pehle ek non-existent test/parity.test.ts ki taraf point karta tha; review mein fix hua).
advantages: Real bugs pakde (precision, 1 ms reset)
Seeded -- har failure replayable
Naye algorithm ke liye reusable
disadvantages: Sampling hai, proof nahi
Sirf forward time aur ek parameter set
Redis zaroori -- bina Redis skip
common_mistakes: Parity ko mocked Redis ke saath chalana (Lua chalti hi nahi)
Sirf allowed path exercise hona aur pass maan lena
Unseeded random -- failure reproduce nahi hota
follow_up_questions: How would you extend the generator to include backward clock jumps and what would you expect to find?
Why compare whole Decision objects with toEqual instead of just allowed?
How does mutation testing complement the parity test?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Real Redis par differential testing sabse strong practical check hai, lekin CI mein Redis chahiye; skip-with-notice honest hai par CI ko Redis dena hi padega warna parity kabhi chalegi nahi.
advanced.failure_scenarios: CI mein Redis na ho toh parity tests chupchaap skip (notice ke saath) -- ek Lua change bina verify ke merge ho sakta hai. Backward time aur extreme parameters par divergence undetected reh sakta hai.
advanced.alternatives: fast-check jaisi property-based library (shrinking ke saath) -- project mein nahi; formal verification (overkill); Lua ko JS mein run karna (fengari) -- real Redis ka tostring behaviour nahi milta.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada algorithms aur parameter grids ke saath steps badhenge; runtime Redis round trips par depend -- parallel keys / pipelines se fast kiya ja sakta hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Generator mein backward jumps, random parameters, aur CI mein Redis service mandatory (skip = fail in CI). (types.ts ka stale 'parity.test.ts' comment already fix ho chuka hai.)
